name: pricing
title: Budget & Pricing
description: Every mention of money — budget, quotes, discount asks, competitor pricing — numbers copied exactly as spoken, plus a quote-anchored read of what kind of pricing signal it is. Call-level budget confirmation and buying authority live in buying_stage and stakeholders, not here.
prompt:
List every mention of money or budget on this call — one entry per distinct mention. An empty list is correct when money never came up; do not stretch non-monetary mentions to fill the list.

For each mention:
- evidence: cite the utterance(s), before you write "text". The line that fixes the pricing_signal read must be among the quotes you cite here.
- text: the mention in the speaker's exact words. CRITICAL: copy numbers character-for-character exactly as the transcript renders them — if it says "forty" write "forty", if it says "40" write "40". Converting between digits and number words will cause the claim to be rejected by verification.
- kind: the single closest fit — budget (their spending capacity), quote (a price offered), discount_request, competitor_price, price_objection, other.
- pricing_signal: the buying signal the mention carries, judged by an observable cue in the quote. sticker_shock = the buyer reacts to a price with surprise or resistance ("that's a lot", "whoa"); comparison = the buyer weighs it against another price or option; packaging_confusion = the buyer asks how tiers, seats, or bundling work; discount_request = the buyer asks for a lower price or a deal; competitor_price_cited = the buyer quotes a competitor's price; none = a neutral money mention carrying no such signal. Use "unclear" when a quote does not settle it.

When a criterion is not clearly met, assign "unclear" rather than the more eventful reading.
